hook: Ride the tiger home with Manikanta and the tigress milk!
how: Tap anywhere to jump, and tap again in the air for a second jump. Jump over thorn bushes, rocks and logs, collect the milk pots and golden bells, and ride all the way to the palace of Pandalam. Lose all three hearts and Manikanta rests a moment, then rides on.
fact: The queen of Pandalam was told only tigress milk could cure her. Young Manikanta went into the forest alone and came back riding a tiger.

hook: Keep the Irumudi steady on the steep climb of Neelimala!
how: The bundle on the swami's head tips with the wind and the slope. Hold the other side of the screen to push it back. Keep the marker in the green zone to walk faster and earn Sharanam bells; tip too far and the swami stops to fix it. Reach the top of Neelimala.
fact: Neelimala is the steepest climb on the way from the Pamba to the temple. The Irumudi on the head must never touch the ground.

hook: Turn the path stones and join the Pamba to the temple!
how: Tap a path stone to turn it. Join the path from the river at the bottom left to the temple at the top right; joined stones glow gold and the swami walks up. Three hills, each bigger. Fewer turns earn more stars.
fact: The traditional forest path from Erumeli runs for over 40 km. Most pilgrims today walk the last 5 km uphill from Pamba.

hook: Float a lamp down the holy river Pamba at night!
how: Slide your finger left and right and the floating lamp follows. Keep away from rocks, logs and the banks: each knock dims the flame. Gather lotus petals and bring the lamp to the ghat with its flame still burning.
fact: The Pamba is called the Dakshina Ganga. On Pamba Vilakku night, lamps are floated on the river.

hook: Slide the tiles and rebuild the 18 holy steps!
how: Tap a tile next to the empty space to slide it. Rebuild three paintings: two 3×3 and one 4×4. Press and hold the small picture to peek at the answer. Fewer moves earn more stars.
fact: Only a swami who has kept the 41-day vow and carries the Irumudi climbs the 18 steps. On the way down, swamis walk backwards, facing Swami.

hook: Learn the Sabarimala route stop by stop, then walk it home from memory!
how: Way up: tap the ten stops in order, from Erumeli to the temple, and read each one's story. Way home: walk back from the temple to Erumeli with the names hidden. Lamps: watch the stops light up and tap them in the same order.
fact: The old route, the Peruvazhi, passes Erumeli, Kalaketti, the Azhutha river, Kallidumkunnu, Karimala, Pamba, Neelimala, Sabari Peedam and Saramkuthi.

hook: Match the symbols of Hari, Hara and Ayyappa!
how: Tap two cards to turn them over. Find the same symbol twice and the pair stays open with a short story about it. Two boards: 6 pairs, then 10 pairs. Fewer turns earn more stars.
fact: Ayyappa is Harihara Sudhan, the son of Hari (Vishnu, as Mohini) and Hara (Shiva).

hook: Wave the aarti lamp in gentle circles with the temple bell!
how: Put your finger on the aarti plate and move it round the circle, clockwise, staying close to the moving golden spark. Each full circle rings the bell. Three rounds, each a little faster.
fact: At dusk the lamp is waved before Swami: the Deeparadhana. At night the temple closes with the lullaby Harivarasanam.

hook: Choose kindness on the Sabarimala path and make your lamp shine!
how: Read eight moments from the pilgrimage and tap the choice you think is right and kind. Each good choice makes the lamp of dharma brighter, with a short note on why.
fact: Ayyappa is also Dharma Sastha, the teacher of what is right. At the temple is written Tat Tvam Asi: That thou art.

hook: Bounce from rock to rock up the hill to the temple!
how: The swami jumps by himself each time he lands. Hold the left or right side of the screen to move him. Ring the golden bells, light the lamps (safe points) and reach the temple at the top. Fall and you start again from the last lamp.
fact: Sabarimala is named after Sabari, the forest devotee who waited for Lord Rama. It stands about 914 m above the sea in the Periyar Tiger Reserve.

hook: Bell, chenda, conch, cymbals: echo the temple rhythm back!
how: Watch and listen as the bell, chenda drum, conch and cymbals play a pattern, then tap them in the same order. Each round adds one more sound. Reach 9 sounds to finish.
fact: On the way, one swami calls "Swamiye!" and all answer "Sharanam Ayyappa!". This call and answer is the Sharanam vili.

hook: Spot the differences at the palace where Manikanta grew up!
how: Look at the two paintings of the Pandalam palace and tap anything that is different, on either picture. Find 5 differences in each of the 2 paintings. A hint glows if you are stuck.
fact: King Rajasekhara of Pandalam found a baby with a bell (mani) at his neck by the Pamba and named him Manikanta.

hook: Piece together Sabarimala, one jigsaw piece at a time!
how: Drag a piece from the tray onto the board and drop it near its place; it snaps in. Three pictures with 9, 12 and 16 pieces. The faint picture on the board helps you.
fact: The temple opens for the 41-day Mandala season and for Makaravilakku in January, plus the first days of each Malayalam month.

hook: Chant the 108 names of Ayyappa, bead by bead on the mala!
how: Tap or swipe the mala to move one bead, and read the name that appears: "Om … Namah". Names show in Sanskrit with Kannada or Telugu script and English letters. A bell rings every 27 names. Tap "Chant for me" to let it move by itself.
fact: A japa mala has 108 beads. The swami wears the mala for the whole 41-day vrata.
